sub_graphs.description: Models how transaction revert affects account deletion

nodes.description: Transaction has touched accounts marked for deletion

nodes.description: Transaction execution fails and reverts

ambiguities.text: The definition of 'touched' includes 'zero-value transfers' but does not clarify if failed calls also count as touches.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume successful and failed calls that access an account both count as 'touches' for cleanup purposes.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'No account may change state from non-existent to existent-but-empty' does not specify enforcement mechanism.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the protocol simply prevents the state transition by not creating the account if it would result in an empty state.

ambiguities.text: Interaction between nonce increment and revert is not explicitly specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume if CREATE reverts, the nonce increment is also reverted along with all other state changes.

implicit_assumptions.description: All client implementations track touched accounts consistently during transaction execution.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Different clients may produce different state roots if touch tracking varies.

implicit_assumptions.description: The state trie can efficiently handle account deletion operations at transaction end.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Inefficient deletion could cause performance issues or DoS vectors.

implicit_assumptions.description: Miner rewards and SUICIDE operations are correctly identified as account touches.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Empty accounts created via these mechanisms might not be cleaned up properly.
